column1: # Known open faults: tests that state the right behaviour and fail while the fault is there.
# Each one is #[ignore]d, so no other tier runs it. The nightly tier (scripts/check.sh nightly) runs
# them alone, by exact name. Its receipt (scripts/lib/nightly-receipt.py) reads a failure as a known
# open fault, counted and named on its own line. A pass is red, "known fault no longer reproduces":
# the fix removes its line here. A test missing from here, or one not #[ignore]d, fails as any other.
# A cut that claims full correctness needs this list empty (benches/fast/release_gate.py verdict
# Rust tests only: an outside check's difference (scripts/check.sh nightly-outside) is never listed, it is red until fixed.
# One line each: the test (binary id, a space, its path in the binary), a tab, what is wrong.

column2: Declaring owl:sameAs an owl:IrreflexiveProperty is accepted, though every term is the same as itself, so the data have no model.
A functional property's two forms of one value (an integer and a decimal) are equated within a commit, but not carried into a later one (docs/limits.md#two-spellings-across-commits).
Under owl2-ql, a clash of an n-ary owl:AllDisjointClasses or owl:AllDisjointProperties isn't found: the commit is applied and the store reads consistent.
